bugs.what: Hearthlands/Tithing never exposed an explicit 'settle this hold's grief' action/location the way every other hold did (Fenmarch's bell, Thornwold's tree-names, Wardmoor's oath-stone). I fully completed 'The Tithe Question' and 'The Almoner's Ledger' there but the 'Hollows rested' counter never incremented for it, and I could not find a granary-interior or equivalent grief site despite the barn being made 'common.'

Several late-game 'weigh what this grief asks' free entries (a great, load-bearing UX feature) were inconsistently present — present at Fenmarch, Thornwold, Wardmoor's core grief rooms, but absent at Tithing's edge/granary steps where it was most needed to orient the player.

Picked-up mystery clue items (e.g. 'notched belt knife' pointing to 'the Broken Bridge, west') were never resolvable within the areas I explored, leaving a dangling thread with no way to know if it was missable content or a bug.
bugs.where: The Split Oak / Ashwood, item: notched belt knife

confusions: Whether Hearthlands counted as one of the 3 required 'hollows rested' was never confirmed — I completed two substantial hold-defining quests there but the status screen's counter suggested it did not count, with no in-game explanation of why.

The distinction between a hold's 'companion side-quests' and its one canonical 'hold grief' (the thing that increments the hollows counter) is not signposted up front — it only becomes clear in retrospect by seeing which quests are literally tagged '(this hold's grief)'.

Early on it wasn't obvious that recruiting a second/third/fourth companion had no party-size cap ('everyone who will come may come') — I braced for a hard choice between companions that never came, which was a pleasant surprise but not something the game told me in advance.
suggestions: Tag every hold's core grief location/action explicitly (like the '(this hold's grief)' quest-name tag) so players can tell at a glance whether a given resolution counts toward the 3-hollows requirement.
Always surface a 'weigh what this grief asks' free entry at a hold's very first named location, not just at the eventual grief-site, so players can route-plan before sinking 40-70 turns into a hold.

Consider a lightweight 'loose threads' summary (status already lists open quests, but a note on which are hold-critical vs. flavor-only would help pacing decisions given 15 holds and a wide turn budget).

The 'name it' / 'read outright' Scholar-class instant-resolution options against hostile guardians were excellent — more classes could benefit from similarly flavorful, class-specific non-combat outs.
